Fit an oblique classification tree based on support vector machines

Source: R/stree.R
stree.Rd

stree() grows a binary classification tree in which every internal node's split is defined by a support vector machine (SVM) hyperplane rather than a threshold on a single variable. When the response has more than two classes, every class is tried in turn as a one-vs-rest binary problem at each node, and the hyperplane that minimizes the chosen impurity measure is kept as the split, following the 'STree' algorithm of Montanana, Gamez and Puerta (2021).

stree(
  formula,
  data,
  kernel = c("linear", "polynomial", "radial"),
  max_depth = 5,
  min_samples = 5,
  impurity_measure = c("entropy", "gini"),
  cost = 1,
  class_order_method = c("natural", "frequency", "original"),
  tie_break_method = c("first", "last", "random"),
  scale = TRUE,
  verbose = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

formula

A stats::formula of the form response ~ predictors, e.g. Species ~ .. Predictors may be numeric, integer, factor or character; the response is coerced to a factor.

data

A data frame containing the variables named in formula.

kernel

Kernel used to fit every node's SVM: one of "linear" (default), "polynomial" or "radial".

max_depth

Maximum depth of the tree (root is depth 1).

min_samples

Minimum number of observations required in a node, and in each of its children, for a split to be attempted. Nodes with fewer observations become leaves.

impurity_measure

Impurity measure used to score one-vs-rest splits at multi-class nodes: "entropy" (default) or "gini".

cost

The SVM regularization parameter C, passed on to e1071::svm().

class_order_method

How the fixed class ordering used internally is determined: "natural" (sorted, default), "frequency" (most frequent class first) or "original" (order of first appearance in data).

tie_break_method

How ties between equally good one-vs-rest splits are broken: "first" (default), "last" or "random".

scale

Logical; if TRUE (default), predictors are centered and scaled to unit variance before each node's SVM is fit, using statistics estimated from that node's own training data and re-applied at prediction time.

verbose

Logical; if TRUE, progress information is reported with base::message() while the tree is grown.

...

Further arguments passed on to e1071::svm(), for example gamma or degree when kernel = "radial" or "polynomial".

Value

An object of class "stree": a list with the fitted tree structure (tree) and the metadata (call, terms, xlevels, levels, response_name) needed by predict.stree(), print.stree() and summary.stree().

References

Montanana, R., Gamez, J. A., Puerta, J. M. (2021). STree: A Single Multi-class Oblique Decision Tree Based on Support Vector Machines. In Advances in Artificial Intelligence, LNAI 12882, Springer. doi:10.1007/978-3-030-85713-4_6

Examples

fit <- stree(Species ~ ., data = iris, max_depth = 3)
fit
#> STree oblique classification tree
#> Call:  stree(formula = Species ~ ., data = iris, max_depth = 3)
#> Classes: setosa, versicolor, virginica 
#> Kernel: linear
#> 
#>  [Node] depth = 1 | n = 150 | kernel = linear | split: setosa vs rest | impurity = 0.6667
#>  |- Positive branch (distance > 0):
#> |   [Leaf] predict = setosa | n = 50
#>  `- Negative branch (distance <= 0):
#>     [Node] depth = 2 | n = 100 | kernel = linear
#>     |- Positive branch (distance > 0):
#>    |   [Leaf] predict = versicolor | n = 46
#>     `- Negative branch (distance <= 0):
#>        [Leaf] predict = virginica | n = 54
predict(fit, iris[1:5, ])
#> [1] setosa setosa setosa setosa setosa
#> Levels: setosa versicolor virginica
predict(fit, iris[1:5, ], type = "prob")
#>      setosa versicolor virginica
#> [1,]      1          0         0
#> [2,]      1          0         0
#> [3,]      1          0         0
#> [4,]      1          0         0
#> [5,]      1          0         0
